Resolve a hostname.

## Synopsis

```text
resolve [client=<client>] [fd=<fd>] [storage=<storage>] [sd=<sd>]
        [<hostname> ...]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Shows the IP addresses a host name resolves to. Without client= or storage= the Director resolves the name itself; with client= (or fd=) the File Daemon resolves it, with storage= the Storage Daemon, and the Director prints their answer. This helps to locate name resolution problems on either side of a connection. Several host names may be given; nothing is changed.

When the Director resolves itself and a name fails, the command stops there and later names are not tried. Without any argument there is no output.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  |  | Resolve on this client. |
| `fd=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  |  | Client name (as client=). |
| `storage=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  |  | Resolve on this storage. |
| `sd=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  |  | Storage name (as storage=). |
| `<hostname>` | string |  |  | repeatable, positional | Host name to resolve. |

## Examples

Addresses as seen by the Director:

```text
resolve backup.example.com
```

How the File Daemon resolves the Director host:

```text
resolve client=bareos-fd backup.example.com
```
